name: Environmental Restoration and Rehabilitation grants
summary: Grants of AUD 150,000 to 350,000 over 3 to 5 years for community groups, Aboriginal organisations, councils and others to protect and restore ecosystems and biodiversity across New South Wales.
reporting: Grantees submit a milestone report after each stage of works in their workplan.

steps: Application through the Grant Management System
Consult NSW staff first for threatened species or ecological communities

eligibility.rule: Has an active Australian Business Number (ABN)
Universities apply only for projects on their own land
Unincorporated community groups partner with an eligible external grant manager
Submit no more than two applications per organization
Allocate at least 10% of the overall project budget to monitoring
Projects using Aboriginal knowledge or practices partner with relevant Aboriginal groups or stakeholders
Activities are not solely for aesthetics, local amenity or recreation

status.quote: The 2026 round closed on 13 May 2026. The program will reopen in April 2027.

applicant_types.quote: incorporated community organisations and associations non-commercial cooperatives local councils local Aboriginal land councils and registered Indigenous corporations universities for projects on their own land state government agencies and entities

geography.quote: projects that protect, conserve and restore the NSW environment

access.quote: Applicants submitted their applications through the Grant Management System.

window.quote: The 2026 round closed on 13 May 2026. The program will reopen in April 2027.

amount.quote: grants between $150,000 and $350,000, with a project duration of 3 to 5 years

reporting.quote: You will need to submit a Milestone report (formerly progress report) after each stage of works that aligns with your approved Workplan.

effort.quote: Applicants submitted their applications through the Grant Management System.
2026 –27 round closes at 11:59 pm on 13 May 2026.

Discuss your project with a departmental staff member before you put in your grant application. In your application, you will need to include the staff officer’s name and confirmation of your discussions.

eligibility.quote: with a project duration of 3 to 5 years
All applicants must have an active Australian Business Number (ABN) to confirm their eligibility as an organisation.
universities (only eligible to apply for funding for projects on their own land)
Unincorporated community organisations can apply for grant funding only if they partner with an eligible organisation, referred to as an ‘external manager’.
Organisations can submit up to 2 applications.
At least 10% of the overall project budget must be allocated to monitoring activities

If your project specifically incorporates Aboriginal knowledge or practices, it is mandatory that you partner with relevant Aboriginal organisations or stakeholders, and this partnership must be demonstrated in your application.
Activities focused solely on improving aesthetics, local amenity, or recreational opportunities, such as gardening or grounds management, are not eligible for funding

after_award.quote: You must submit a milestone report after each stage of work (usually every 12 months) through the online Grant Management System (GMS).
provide milestone reports in accordance with the milestone payment and reporting schedule in the funding agreement

documents.quote: You must provide relevant mapping information when applying for funding.
CVs and profiles for all staff who will play an active role in the project.
Include management plans that your project aligns with or contributes to.
Applicants are required to show evidence of meaningful consultation, such as letters of support from the appropriate Aboriginal stakeholders.

documents: Relevant project maps, including site maps where sites are known
CVs and profiles for staff active in the project
Management plans the project aligns with or contributes to, where applicable
Evidence of meaningful Aboriginal consultation for projects using Aboriginal knowledge or practices
